questions.prompt: What does 'the tests are the outermost circle' mean?

options.text: Tests are the most important business rules
Tests are the most peripheral, detailed part: they depend inward on everything, and nothing depends on them
Tests belong in the entities layer

questions.explanation: Tests are like another driving adapter — the outermost circle. They depend inward on the system, and nothing depends on them.

questions.prompt: How should you test a business rule quickly and reliably?

options.text: By driving the use case's port directly with a request model and in-memory doubles
By connecting to the production database

questions.explanation: Driving the use-case port with doubles is fast, deterministic, and focused on the rule — no UI, HTTP, or real database involved.

questions.prompt: A test that breaks due to changes unrelated to its intent (e.g., coupling to exact SQL or over-specified mock calls) is called a ______ test.
questions.explanation: Fragile tests come from coupling to volatile details; testing through stable boundaries and asserting state keeps tests robust.

questions.prompt: Match each test double to its description.

pairs.right: Returns canned answers to provide inputs
A working but simplified implementation (e.g., in-memory repo)
Verifies it was called in an expected way

questions.explanation: Stubs feed inputs, fakes are simplified working implementations, and mocks assert interactions. Prefer state-based tests with stubs/fakes over heavy mocking.

questions.prompt: Order the testing pyramid from the widest base (most tests) to the narrow top (fewest).
questions.explanation: Many fast unit tests form the base, some integration tests in the middle, and few slow end-to-end tests at the top.

questions.prompt: Which are sound testing practices in a clean architecture? Select all that apply.

options.text: Test use cases at their ports with in-memory fakes
Keep end-to-end tests few and focused on critical paths
Use a real production database for every unit test
Prefer state-based assertions over over-specified mock interactions

questions.explanation: Test rules at ports with fakes, keep e2e tests few, and prefer state assertions. Using a real database for every unit test is slow and non-deterministic, and over-mocking makes tests fragile.
